newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - soft, looking for action.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - soft, looking for action.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices were unchanged to a touch softer in becalmed, early afternoon trade on Tuesday that was notable for the paucity of new issues and secondary market supplies.
"I'd say it's sort of on the soft side, no great shakes," said a trader, adding prices on some issues might have eased around an eighth of a point.
The Standard and Poor's Corp Blue list remained below the $1 billion mark, signaling lean inventories. On Tuesday, the yardstick of the secondary market stood at almost $955 million.

The apparent reluctance of new issuers to jump in, despite a recent, sizable rise in bond prices, baffled some participants, who were at a loss to explain why more issuers did not seem to capitalizing on the lower rates, though they noted volumes often fall in summer. "You'd think there'd be more coming in, wouldn't you," another trader said.
The 30-day visible supply of upcoming municipal bond sales was $6.424 billion as of July 14, up $376 million from Friday, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated sales were expected to total $4.317 billion in 68 issues and competitive bond sales added up to $2.106 billion in 142 issues.
Reuters visible supply counts all deals underwriters have either scheduled for sale in the next 30 business days, or have said they tentatively plan to price during the period.
On Tuesday, municipal bond sales were expected to total $1.1 billion in 48 sales. The list of negotiated offerings hit $767 million in 16 sales.
The New York State Metropolitan Transportation Authority sold $249 million of revenue bonds, which were priced with a top yield of 5.45 percent in 2024.
And Pennsylvania Housing Finance Agency sold $75 million of revenue bonds, which fetched 5.80 percent in 2029.

On the competitive side, 32 sales totaling $363 million were scheduled. A three-part $130.5 million Virginia HDA offering at 1130 EDT was the largest. A total of $78.5 million of revenue bonds were won by Bankers Trust Securities and not reoffered.

The latest data on retail sales in June, which rose 0.5 percent, higher than the 0.2 percent rise that was predicted, initally weighed on fixed-income markets. But a downward revision in May sales, which were changed to down 0.3 percent from 0.1 percent, undercut the bearishness of the June data.

In Chicago futures markets, September municipal bond futures slipped six ticks to 119-6/32, and September Treasury bond futures fell seven ticks to 113-23/32. This left the MOB spread at 175 ticks, little changed.
In the secondary market, Dade County, Florida, Water and Sewer System Revenues of 2021, which pay a 5-1/4 percent coupon, were offered at 5.38 percent, NET, unchanged.
And Orange Coutny, Florida, School Board Certificates of Participation, which carry a 5-3/8 percent coupon, were offered at 99-1/2, unchanged.
